slides.headline: GOOGLE'S AI FILMED A COUPLE'S FIRST MEETING USING ZERO SECONDS OF REAL FOOTAGE.
slides.image_prompt: Sundar Pichai waist-up holding a crumbling black-and-white photograph in one hand and a phone with the Google logo showing the same scene vivid in warm amber in the other, jaw dropped in disbelief, Google blue flooding the studio wall behind him, documentary press photo, 35mm, extremely realistic and shocking.

slides.headline: IF A MOMENT WAS NEVER FILMED, IT WAS GONE FOREVER
slides.body:
That was the rule everyone believed.

You could describe it. You could write it down. But you could never actually see it again.

Google just broke that rule

slides.headline: GOOGLE STUDIED OLD PHOTOS OF TWO REAL PEOPLE
slides.body:
Burt and Ethelle. A real couple, their story only captured in old photos.

Google's AI studied those photos and learned exactly how each of them moved.

Imagine watching your grandparents' first meeting on screen

slides.headline: ZERO SECONDS OF REAL FOOTAGE EXISTS
slides.body: The AI learned their exact movements from photos instead

slides.headline: HOW AI BROUGHT BACK A LOST MOMENT
slides.body: Old photos taught the AI how they moved It copied their exact micro-expressions from those photos Documentary 'Love, Rendered' now live on YouTube 208.9K views on X in under 27 hours

slides.headline: EVERY PHOTO IS NOW A VIDEO WAITING TO EXIST
slides.body:
Your old photos can now become real video, no camera crew.

The tech that was supposed to make things feel fake just brought back the most human moment ever

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: GOOGLE'S AI FILMED A MOMENT NO CAMERA EVER CAUGHT
slides.body: AI learned how Burt and Ethelle moved from old photos 'Love, Rendered': full documentary, live on YouTube 208.9K views on X in under 27 hours Send this to someone whose family was never filmed

caption:
Swipe to see how Google's AI turned old photos into a documentary of a real couple's first meeting that was never filmed 🎞

The belief that lost moments stay gone forever, how Google DeepMind studied a real couple named Burt and Ethelle from restored archival photos, how its AI learned their exact movements and micro-expressions, what it built: a full documentary called Love, Rendered on YouTube, the fact that zero footage ever existed of the moments it recreated, and the 208.9K views the post earned on X in under 27 hours.

AI just proved that any moment only captured in photos can now be turned into video. First meetings, weddings, goodbyes. The line between filmed and unfilmed just disappeared.

Running a business? DM us 'AI' and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: Google DeepMind on X, Sep 11 2026
